title: Barren Women and Promised Sons
lead: Again and again the Bible tells of a woman who cannot have children until God intervenes, and of the special son she then bears: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Manoah's wife, Hannah, the Shunammite woman and Elizabeth.

sections.b: Sarah was barren (Genesis 11:30) until Isaac was promised and born (Genesis 18:10–14; 21:1–3). Rebekah conceived after Isaac prayed (Genesis 25:21), and Rachel after God "remembered" her (Genesis 30:22). Manoah's wife received an angel's promise of Samson (Judges 13:2–3), Hannah prayed for Samuel at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1:2–20), and Elisha promised the Shunammite woman a son (2 Kings 4:14–17). In the New Testament, Elizabeth bears John the Baptist (Luke 1:7, 13). The pattern shows that the child is God's gift, born for a purpose. Isaiah turns it into a picture of Zion: "Sing, barren woman" (Isaiah 54:1), which Paul applies to the church (Galatians 4:27). Readers today also note the pain these stories record, and that the Bible does not treat barrenness as a sign of sin in these women.
sections.refs: Genesis 11:30; Genesis 18:10–14; Genesis 25:21; Genesis 30:22; Judges 13:2–3; 1 Samuel 1:2–20; 2 Kings 4:14–17; Luke 1:7; Isaiah 54:1; Galatians 4:27
